subject: Partial output coherence in streaming demo — model recommendations & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Partial output coherence in streaming demo — model recommendations & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a focused evaluation started:

What we saw (recap)
- Partial output slices during streaming where the model stops mid-sentence and resumes with unrelated content a few tokens later.
- Stop-sequence behavior seemed to trigger on punctuation in structured medical notes (period + newline).
- Latency for long contexts (~6k tokens) spiked past what you considered acceptable for the UI.

My read / immediate recommendations
- Run a short, targeted streaming-quality eval on a representative prompt set (attached) and the demo recording you shared.
- Test three candidate model configurations: rw-llama-13b-inf (Redwood-optimized 13B), rw-opt-2.7b-q4 (quantized candidate), and an open baseline (vicuna-7b). We should compare coherence and token latency.
- Try adjusting stop-sequence sets (add explicit \"\n\" and line-break tokens) and enable prefix KV-caching where possible.

What I’m proposing (next steps)
1) Can you upload the anonymized example prompts and the short transcript you mentioned to the Drive folder I linked below? That will let us reproduce the streaming behavior.
2) With your go-ahead we’ll run a 48-hour eval using your samples and the three model configs, then share a short report (quality + perf + recommended config).
3) Schedule a 30-min sync after we have results — proposed window: next Thursday 10–12 PT.

Attachments included: prompt-set-v1.txt (sample prompts), streaming-benchmarks-2027.csv (example output format), medicomp-demo-recording.mp4 (your demo recording stub referenced)

Drive upload link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xY_demo-sample-upload
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/contacts/54672

If that plan looks good I’ll kick off the eval once you confirm upload and give permission to run against the samples.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Partial output coherence in streaming demo — model recommendations & next steps

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the recap. I uploaded two items to the Drive folder: medicomp_example_prompt.txt and a short snippet of the live trace we captured. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xY_demo-sample-upload (same folder)

Couple of notes from our side:
- The most visible issue is intermittent truncation: the model emits a partial sentence, then after ~200–500ms emits a continuation that seems contextually disconnected. Example (from transcript):
  Prompt: \"Generate a concise discharge summary for patient X with diabetes and hypertension.\"
  Output chunk 1: \"Patient X, a 62-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes...\"
  (pause / new chunk)
  Output chunk 2: \"— recommended follow up: refer to cardiology for...\"
  That mid-sentence jump loses the connective tissue and looks like two different completions stitched together.
- Stop sequence oddity: when our UI sends a double-newline (\"\n\n\") as the end-of-turn marker the model sometimes treats the period before the newline as a stop trigger.
- Latency: with our default 6k token context the per-token emission latency climbs and the UI shows a noticeable stutter after the first 600 tokens.

We’re happy for you to run the eval. Please use the sample prompts I uploaded and ping me once you have initial results.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Medicomp
alex@medicomp.ai

Thanks Priya — I can take point on the eval. Quick technical plan and thresholds so we’re aligned before we start: 

Planned tests
- Reproduce streaming with the Medicomp samples (they already uploaded). We'll run the three model configs in parallel on identical infra to avoid routing variance.
- Emission settings: 1) baseline (current defaults), 2) adjusted stop set (include explicit LF token and two-token end marker), 3) chunked streaming (emit every 16–32 tokens with prefix KV caching enabled).
- Context lengths: 2k, 4k, 6k, 8k tokens.

Metrics (first-pass thresholds)
- Median token emission latency: target < 120 ms
- Coherence continuity score (internal metric, see link): target >= 0.95 on provided prompt set
- Stop-trigger false positive rate: < 2%
- Partial-chunk mismatches (where chunk boundary creates discontinuity): aim to reduce by 90% vs their demo trace

Artifacts we’ll produce
- Per-model CSV (sample outputs + per-token latencies) [streaming-benchmarks-2027.csv]
- Short write-up with recommended model and recommended stop-sequence config
- Short recording demonstrating the fixed streaming flow

We’ll start the runs first thing Wednesday (2027-06-02 08:00 PT) and aim to have the first-pass report by EOD Wednesday. If infra needs crop up I’ll flag Sergio.

Attachment: benchmark-plan.md (test steps + infra checklist)

-Neha
